response.sql:
WITH behaviour_trader_link AS (
  SELECT 
    ab.abhvreg,
    t.tradekind
  FROM advancedbehavior ab
  INNER JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg
  INNER JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg
),
type_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    tradekind,
    COUNT(*) as type_count
  FROM behaviour_trader_link
  GROUP BY tradekind
),
statistics AS (
  SELECT 
    tc.tradekind,
    tc.type_count,
    tc.type_count::numeric / SUM(tc.type_count)::numeric OVER () as share,
    1::numeric / COUNT(*)::numeric OVER () as avg_share
  FROM type_counts tc
)
SELECT 
  tradekind,
  type_count,
  share,
  share - avg_share as excess
FROM statistics
WHERE share > avg_share
ORDER BY excess DESC;

assumptions.assumption: NULL values in tradekind are treated as a separate group, per the phrase 'missing type as its own group'. SQL GROUP BY treats NULL as a distinct value.
INNER JOINs drop behaviour records without a matching transaction record or transaction records without a matching trader, implementing 'exact text matches and drop anything without a match'.
The 'plain average of the per-type shares' is the arithmetic mean: 1/(number of distinct trader types in the result). Mathematically, this equals (sum of all shares) / (count of types), which is 1/n.
